I traced the whole path but could not prove the exact cause. The bug file has only one sentence and doesn't say what the icon actually showed, so I can't tell which of two explanations fits.

## Findings

**The app picks the right card and worktree.** The active schedule service (`app/src/services/actions/active_schedule_service.ts:253-259`) maps only the current card (`cardInternalIds[currentIndex]`) to the sequence's `checkoutPath` and `expectedBranch`. A test already confirms that card 2 takes over from card 1 (`active_schedule_service.node.test.ts:111-112`). The data on disk is also consistent: the schedule has `currentIndex: 1` and `expectedBranch` set to the card-2 branch, and `git worktree list` shows `dev2` on that same branch.

**The worktree list in the app falls behind the branch switches.** `sequenceWorktreeAssignment` (`app/src/components/sequence_worktree_assignment.ts:13-14`) finds the worktree by path. It then checks that the branch checked out there equals `expectedBranch`. That branch comes from the desktop worktree service. The desktop only refreshes this list on a 5-second timer or when `requireLinkedCheckout` runs. A `git switch` does not trigger a refresh, because `runGit` in `desktop/src/git/worktree_service.js` only runs an ownership check for that command.

**Moving to card 2 involves more branch switches than starting card 1.** When card 1 finishes, `SequenceWorktreeExecution.integrateNow` switches the checkout from the card-1 branch to the sequence branch. Then `ScheduledCardSequenceEngine.advanceOrCompleteNow` saves `currentIndex + 1`. After that, `prepareNow` switches again with `git switch -c` to the card-2 branch. Each of these steps saves a new `expectedBranch` to the schedule file before the desktop has re-read the worktree's branch. So for card 2, the app compares the new `expectedBranch` with an old branch for a while, and the indicator shows "Sequence worktree changed branch" in red. Card 1 starts from the parking branch, which the app already knows, so it shows the right worktree straight away.

**What I could not confirm.** The refresh inside `SequenceWorktreeExecution.context` and the 5-second timer should eventually correct the display. There is one gap: `refreshLocal` reuses a refresh that is already running, and that refresh may have read the branch before the switch. Even then, the next timer tick should fix it. A problem that never goes away (for example, "P" or the wrong number staying for the whole run) would need a different cause, and I found no code path that produces one.

## Proposed solution

After every `git switch` in `SequenceWorktreeExecution`, refresh that one worktree record before saving the new `expectedBranch`. That covers `createBranch` and the switch-to-target step in `integrateNow`. The desktop already has `worktreeService.refreshRecordAfterMutation(project, checkoutPath)` for this. This way the app never receives an `expectedBranch` that is ahead of the branch it knows about. A regression test in `sequence_worktree_execution.test.mjs` should check that the record refresh runs before the save that changes `expectedBranch`.

Before I write this into the design document: what exactly did the card-2 icon show (a red number, "?", "P", or a different number), and did it correct itself after a few seconds? If it corrected itself, the fix above covers it. If it stayed wrong, I need to dig further.

> and the 5-second timer should eventually correct the display

It's a polling loop in the desktop worktree service, `desktop/src/git/worktree_service.js`. It is not something I added or am proposing.

**What it is.** `REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 5000` is set at `desktop/src/git/worktree_service.js:10`. The loop works like this:

- `startProject` (line 130) runs `refreshLocal()` once when a project opens.
- `refreshLocal` (line 844) runs `performRefresh`. In its `finally` block it calls `scheduleRefresh()` (lines 857-858).
- `scheduleRefresh` (line 919) sets a 5-second `setTimeout` that calls `refreshLocal()` again.

So while a project is open, the desktop re-reads the worktree state every 5 seconds. `refreshAfterMutation` and `refreshRecordAfterMutation` restart the same timer after an explicit worktree change. `stopProject` stops it.

**What it does.** Each refresh calls `primaryRepositoryStatus` and `readWorktreeRecords`. These read `git worktree list` plus each worktree's branch and status (valid, dirty, and so on). If the result differs from the last state, `publish` sends it to the app through `onWorktreesChanged`. In the app, `WorktreeService.handleState` (`app/src/services/project/worktree_service.ts:560`) updates its records and fires `recordsChanged` or `recordChanged`. The card worktree indicator listens for those events through `useOpenWorktrees`.

**Why it matters for B_312.** Polling is the only thing that picks up a branch change made by a plain `git switch`. Nothing pushes an update when the sequence switches branches. So after the sequence changes `expectedBranch`, the app can keep seeing the old branch for up to about 5 seconds, until the next poll. That's why I said the display should correct itself after a while. It also means the fix I proposed (refreshing the record right after each switch) doesn't depend on this timer.
> The card worktree indicator listens for those events through useOpenWorktrees.

That points to the app's copy of the schedules being stale. I'm checking how schedule-file changes reach the app.

entries.content:
I found the cause, and it's in the app, not in the worktree refresh. My earlier explanation (the worktree list falling behind) was wrong. Card 1 still showing worktree 2 rules it out: the app only gives the sequence worktree to the current card. If the app had loaded the new schedule, card 1 would have lost that icon and card 2 would have gained it. So the app is still holding the schedule from when card 1 was running.

## Root cause

`ActiveScheduleService` only reloads schedules when a file-watch event matches the schedules file path (`app/src/services/actions/active_schedule_service.ts:234-238`). It builds the path it compares against from `getActionsFolder()`, which is defined at line 63:

```ts
getActionsFolder: () => configService.getProjectConfig().actionsFolder,
```

`configService.getProjectConfig()` returns the raw config value, and `md2.config.json` has `"actionsFolder": "actions"` and `"projectFolder": "design"`. So the service compares against `actions/.md2-schedules.json`. The desktop watcher reports paths relative to the repository root (`desktop/src/project/project_files.js:514`), so the event path is `design/actions/.md2-schedules.json`. The two never match, and the app never reloads schedules after a file change.

Card 1 only looks right because `card_sequence_registration.ts:24` calls `activeScheduleService.refresh()` once, right after the sequence is registered. Every later change, including the move to card 2, is missed until something else triggers a reload, such as reopening the project.

The rest of the app already joins the two folders. It does this through `resolveProjectConfigPaths` (`app/src/data/data_types.ts:573`), for example in `data_service_context.ts:63` and `project_loading.ts:243`.

## Proposed solution

Change line 63 so the actions folder is joined with the project folder:

```ts
getActionsFolder: () => resolveProjectConfigPaths(configService.getProjectConfig()).actionsFolder,
```

`getActionsFolder` has no other callers, so nothing else is affected. I'd also add a regression test in `active_schedule_service.node.test.ts`. It would use a config where `projectFolder` is `design` and `actionsFolder` is `actions`, send a watch event for `design/actions/.md2-schedules.json`, and check that the schedules reload.

This bug probably also leaves the active schedules panel stale after the first refresh, not just the card icon.

The worktree-refresh fix I proposed earlier isn't needed for this bug, so I'd drop it.

Should I make the fix and add the test?

When the second card started in the sequence, it did not show the correct worktree number in the icon on the card

## Analysis

The app never reloads the schedule list after the first refresh, so the card indicator keeps showing the sequence state from when card 1 was running. Card 1 keeps the sequence worktree, and card 2 never gets it.

* `ActiveScheduleService.handleRepositoryChanged` (`app/src/services/actions/active_schedule_service.ts`) only calls `refresh()` when a watch event path equals `${getActionsFolder()}/.md2-schedules.json`.
* `getActionsFolder` is defined as `configService.getProjectConfig().actionsFolder`. This is the raw config value (`actions`), not joined with `projectFolder` (`design`).
* The desktop watcher (`watchProject` in `desktop/src/project/project_files.js`) reports paths relative to the repository root, so the event path is `design/actions/.md2-schedules.json`. The paths never match, and the app never reloads schedules from watch events.
* Card 1 only looks correct because `card_sequence_registration.ts` calls `activeScheduleService.refresh()` once, right after the sequence is registered.
* The card indicator gets the sequence worktree only for `cardInternalIds[currentIndex]` (`setSchedules`), so a stale `currentIndex` leaves the worktree on card 1.

B\_313 (sequence progress stuck on card 1 in the sequences overview dialog, deleted now) had the same root cause. `active_schedules_dialog.tsx` renders `currentIndex` from the same stale snapshot. This card fixes both bugs.

## Fix

* In `active_schedule_service.ts`, resolve the actions folder the same way the rest of the app does: `getActionsFolder: () => resolveProjectConfigPaths(configService.getProjectConfig()).actionsFolder`. `getActionsFolder` has no other callers.
* Add a regression test in `active_schedule_service.node.test.ts`: with `projectFolder` set to `design` and `actionsFolder` set to `actions`, a watch event for `design/actions/.md2-schedules.json` reloads the schedules, moves the sequence worktree from card 1 to card 2, and advances `currentIndex` in the snapshot (the value behind the B\_313 progress text).

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |
